thread:
maya: FYI seeing a weird sensor 'hum' metric on several gnodes in us-west1. IOPS dropped ~60% and a few GPU attaches failed in the last 30m. Anyone else?
raj: got it. do you have node ids?
maya: gnode-usw1-172, gnode-usw1-188, gnode-usw1-199
ops-bot: Alert: disk-telemetry anomaly in us-west1 — 3 hosts affected. Incident created INC-20260321-83
eli: pinging storage infra. could be thermal ramp or NVMe controller queue stall.
maya: pasting quick dmesg snippet:
```
dmesg | tail -n 50
[12345.678901] nvme0: I/O 0x1a2cd failed, status: media_error
[12345.679001] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 98765432
[12346.001234] blk_mq: latency 1180ms, scheduling stall
```
raj: also seeing blk_mq timeouts and write backlog in iostat (avg await > 900ms).
sophia: can we cordon the three nodes and migrate pending GPU jobs off them?
dan: +1 cordon. plan: swap scratchpool to spares, run nvme SMART, then reprovision a canary GPU.
maya: tentative plan:
1) cordon gnode-usw1-172/188/199
2) drain non-running/queued jobs (keep running prod where possible)
3) re-route batch to us-central if backlog grows
4) run `sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` and `smartctl`
5) canary replace/attach on gnode-usw1-199 first, target rollback window ~5:00 UTC
eli: running smart-log now. command: `sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`
ops-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/storage/nvme-anomaly (follow thermal & media errors section)
eli: smart-log output: critical_warning=1, media_errors=7, temperature=79C, power_cycles=120
maya: 79C temp — thermal spike. ops-team, check CRAC/fan speeds and rack cooling for that pod.
raj: cost question: if we cordon these nodes for 12h we'll create GPU provisioning backlog in us-west1. Spill to us-central for latency-insensitive batch?
sophia: yes but only for batch/non-interactive queues. preserve prod region SLA. also open a ticket with provider on a thermal event for those racks.
dan: doing a canary drive swap on gnode-usw1-199 now; will reattach scratch and try GPU attach in ~10m.
maya: tagging @oncall for coverage during the operation window.
oncall-bot: @oncall scheduled: dan assigned for thread 3838383838 until 3838383850
dan: canary finished: new drive attached, scratchpool rebalanced, GPU attach succeeded on gnode-usw1-199. IOPS back to baseline on that node.
maya: good. remaining two nodes still show elevated media error counters. next steps: replace drives on 172 & 188 during nightly low-traffic window, keep spill plan ready, provider ticket open.
sophia: +1, please create CL with postmortem and remediation checklist once replacements done.
eli: opened PR for remediation checklist: https://redwood.internal/p/rb/1234
maya: closing for now — will reopen if we see regressions :thumbsup:
